songInfo.title: Would?
songInfo.tuning: Half-Step Down (Eb Ab Db Gb Bb Eb)

scalesUsed.notes: F# - G# - A - B - C# - D - E
scalesUsed.application: Drives the haunting, brooding verses and the dark descending harmonic movement
Bedrock for Jerry Cantrell's expressive vocal unisons, wah-wah lead fills, and soaring guitar solo

scalesUsed.notes: F# - A - B - C - C# - E
scalesUsed.application: The flatted 5th (C natural) adds visceral tension to the chromatic chorus passing chords

keyAndScale.keySignature: Three sharps (F#, C#, G#) (concert F minor due to half-step down tuning)
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: F# Minor is the relative minor of A Major

mainProgression.description: Jerry Cantrell's signature Seattle grunge progression. The verse features eerie open-string arpeggios over Mike Starr's hypnotic bassline, before exploding into a devastating chorus featuring a dark Neapolitan bII chord (G major) resolving down to F#m.

sectionProgressions.description: Iconic opening bass riff answered by Cantrell's chiming, chorus-drenched arpeggiated dyads
Brooding two-chord vamp allowing open B and high E strings to ring as dissonant pedal points
'Into the flood again, same old trip it was back then...' - colossal wall of layered Bogner and Marshall tube distortion
Ascending harmonic release introducing Layne Staley's soaring vocal crescendo before the guitar solo

harmonicFunction: F#m (i) - Heavy, resonant tonic minor chord establishing the visceral emotional weight
D (bVI) - Submediant chord providing emotional lift and harmonic expansiveness
G (bII) - Neapolitan chord providing intense chromatic friction that snaps back into the tonic F#m
Bm (iv) - Subdominant minor chord deepening the melancholic bridge texture
E (VII) - Subtonic major chord driving the triumphant turnaround into the chorus climax

techniques.name: Open-String Grunge Arpeggiation
techniques.description: Fretting dark, inverted minor dyad shapes on strings 4 and 3 while letting open strings 2 and 1 ring out, generating eerie dissonance and expansive stereo width

notes: Fret the F# note on fret 4 of the D string and A on fret 2 of the G string
Keep fret-hand fingers arched high so the open B and high E strings ring continuously
Use a smooth down-up picking motion across strings 4, 3, 2, and 1
Slide fret-hand shape up one fret to fret 5 and 4 for the chilling Gadd9 coloration
sequence: Pick string 3, string 2, and string 1 in fluid arpeggiation
Slide up to fret 5 with fingers 3 and 1 intact
Dampen strings slightly on the turnaround with fret-hand pressure release
tips: Engage an analog chorus or flanger pedal with slow rate to give the open strings a swirling, underwater texture
Use the neck pickup on clean and verse passages for warm, woody resonance
Tune carefully: half-step down tuning makes open strings looser and prone to going sharp if fretted too hard

techniques.name: Heavy Downstroke Chunking & Cocked Wah Soloing
techniques.description: Crushing, synchronized downstroke power chord picking in the chorus, transitioning to expressive, vocal wah-wah solo sweeps in the higher register

notes: Deliver heavy, deliberate downstrokes across root, fifth, and octave notes of power chords
Lock precisely with the drum kick and snare on every eighth-note subdivision
For the solo, rock the wah pedal in sync with your vocal phrasing rather than frantic pumping
Dig deep into whole-step blues bends at frets 14 and 16 on the G and B strings
sequence: Smash F#5 power chord downbeat with unmuted sustain
Shift to D5 on the 5th string, then G5 on low E
Engage wah pedal for lead fills at the 14th fret
Execute singing vibrato at the peak of each bend
tips: Jerry Cantrell used a combination of Bogner Fish preamp, Marshall JCM800, and a Dunlop Cry Baby wah
A heavy guitar pick (1.14mm Dunlop Tortex) gives the requisite percussive thump on low power chords
Scoop a little 500Hz from your EQ to leave room for the booming bass tone

sections.name: Intro Hypnotic Bass & Dyad Entry
sections.description: Mike Starr's iconic driving bassline sets the dark mood before Cantrell's chorus-laden guitar dyads chime across the stereo spectrum at 116 BPM.
notes: Let the open high E and B strings ring freely
Light pick attack with subtle chorusing effect
Smooth fret-hand slide from fret 4 to fret 5 on the D string
Lock seamlessly into the 116 BPM pocket

sections.name: Verse 1 Brooding Arpeggios
sections.description: 'Into the flood again, same old trip it was back then...' - haunting guitar arpeggios accompany Layne Staley's commanding vocal.
notes: Keep fingers arched so fretted notes don't mute open strings
Maintain delicate dynamic balance under the vocal
Accentuate the chromatic lift on the G chord
Prepare pick hand for the massive chorus explosion
sections.exerciseLabel: Verse Arpeggio Dynamics & Open String Resonance

sections.name: Chorus Stadium Heavy Distortion
sections.technique: Heavy Downstroke Chunking & Cocked Wah Soloing
sections.description: 'Am I wrong? Have I run too far to get home?' - devastating wall-of-sound power chords explode through high-gain tube amplifiers.
notes: All downstrokes with maximum pick attack
Hit the G5 chord hard to emphasize the Neapolitan chromatic pull
Lock tight with Sean Kinney's explosive snare hits
Sharp mute on the turnaround back to verse

sections.name: Bridge Ascending Release
sections.technique: Heavy Downstroke Chunking & Cocked Wah Soloing
sections.description: Harmonic departure sweeping through D, Bm, and E power chords, setting up the dramatic vocal climax.
notes: Dynamic crescendo across four bars
Slide power chord shapes smoothly along the 5th string
Hold the E5 chord with full sustaining tube feedback
Seamless release into the guitar solo

sections.name: Guitar Solo & Cry Baby Wah Phrasing
sections.technique: Heavy Downstroke Chunking & Cocked Wah Soloing
sections.description: Jerry Cantrell delivers a dark, singing guitar solo using an expressive wah-wah sweep over crying minor pentatonic bends.
notes: Full-step bend on fret 16 of the G string up to F#
Sweep the wah forward on the ascent and pull back on the resolution
Wide vibrato applied with the whole wrist
Soulful blue note on fret 15 of the B string

sections.name: Outro Climax & 'If I Would, Could You?'
sections.technique: Heavy Downstroke Chunking & Cocked Wah Soloing
sections.description: 'If I would, could you?' - thunderous final chorus repetition concluding with an abrupt, monumental unison stop.
notes: Maximum heavy rock energy and pick assault
Full band locks onto the final syncopated hit
Instant silence on the final chord cut-off
Zero decaying trail: punchy, stark finish

guitar.recommended: G&L Rampage or Gibson Les Paul Custom with Seymour Duncan JB bridge humbucker
guitar.pickup: High-output bridge humbucker (Seymour Duncan JB) for biting attack and thick harmonic crunch

amp.recommended: Bogner Fish Preamp through a Mesa/Boogie 2:90 power amp, paired with a Marshall JCM800

effects.distortion: Thick tube distortion combining Bogner preamps and Marshall power sections
effects.other: Dunlop JC95 Jerry Cantrell Signature Cry Baby Wah and Boss CH-1 Super Chorus

beginner.title: Half-Step Down Tuning & Power Chords
steps: Tune your guitar half-step down (Eb Ab Db Gb Bb Eb)
Learn F#5, D5, and G5 power chord voicings
Practice transitioning with steady downstrokes at 116 BPM

intermediate.title: The Open-String Verse Dyads
steps: Fret the F#m and G dyad shapes while letting open B and high E strings ring
Maintain clean string separation without choking adjacent open strings
Execute the dynamic transition from clean verse to roaring chorus

advanced.title: The Wah-Wah Solo & Complete Performance
steps: Transcribe and perform Cantrell's vocal wah-pedal guitar solo
Master the expressive whole-step bends and singing vibrato
Perform the entire track locked with the rhythm section

commonMistakes: Failing to tune down a half step, causing dissonance with the studio recording
Accidentally muting the ringing open B and high E strings during verse arpeggios
Pumping the wah pedal too fast during the solo instead of matching vocal inflections
Rushing the Neapolitan G chord transition in the chorus
practiceRoutine: 5 mins: Half-step down tuning check and finger warm-up
10 mins: Slow verse dyad practice ensuring open strings ring cleanly
10 mins: Chorus downstroke power chord syncopation with metronome at 116 BPM
10 mins: Wah-pedal foot coordination and solo bend accuracy drills
focusAreas: Fret-hand arching to preserve open ringing high strings
Heavy, synchronized downstroke pick attack on power chords
Vocal wah-pedal coordination and expressive wrist vibrato
metronomeWork: Practice the verse arpeggio at 85 BPM with a metronome to guarantee clean note separation
Advance to full tempo of 116 BPM once 4 consecutive flawless cycles are played
Emphasize the heavy downbeat accents on beats 1 and 3 during chorus drills
